name: Dimension Law for Polyhedral Face Classes
statement: If a finite polyhedral cell complex $X$ has at least one vertex and dimension $D$, then $\operatorname{hd}(\mathcal H_X)=D+1$. Moreover $\operatorname{VC}(\mathcal H_X)=D+1$ exactly when $X$ has a $D$-dimensional simplex.
proof: Face intervals have the homology of the appropriate face-figure spheres, so the empty-to-top-cell interval gives projective dimension $D+1$. Shattering $D+1$ vertices forces them to be the vertices of a simplex cell, and a simplex cell visibly shatters its vertices.
